title: Data of a ringed sheaf slice presentation and its exact module adjunctions
statement: Let $C$ be a small category with Grothendieck topology $J$, let $R$ be a sheaf of rings and let $A$ be a sheaf of sets in the common universe [def-weil-size-convention]. Use the element-site constructions of [def-sfb-element-site-localization] and the fibre, set-restriction and direct-sum constructions of [def-sfb-element-site-slice-constructions]. Define ringed sheaf slice adjunction data to consist of the following data and properties, without asserting their existence. Include equality of the element topology with the restricted topology of $p_A$; an equivalence $e:\operatorname{Sh}(J_A)\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(J)/A$ with a natural isomorphism from its inverse followed by the forgetful functor to the fibre presheaf functor; and the formula $R_A=p_A^*R$ on underlying presheaves. Include a ringed-topos morphism $j:(\operatorname{Sh}(J_A),R_A)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(J),R)$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism] whose inverse image equals the sectionwise set restriction, and whose structural map sends each section to that same section under this identification. On module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], include a functor $P:\operatorname{Mod}(R)\to\operatorname{Mod}(R_A)$ (with default the canonical sectionwise module restriction), an adjunction $P\dashv j_*$ and equalities of carriers $(PM)(U,s)=M(U)$. Include a functor $E:\operatorname{Mod}(R_A)\to\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ with, for each $L$, an isomorphism from $EL$ to the module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] of the direct-sum presheaf $U\mapsto\bigoplus_{s\in A(U)}L(U,s)$, an adjunction $E\dashv P$, preservation of finite limits and finite colimits by both $P$ and $E$, and additivity of $E$. Finally, for every sheaf map $b:B\to A$, include continuity of its element-site functor and a module restriction functor equal to the canonical restriction along that functor, an equivalence $\operatorname{Sh}(J_B)\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(J)/B$, and a natural isomorphism between $P$ followed by this restriction and the canonical sectionwise restriction from $R$ to $R_B$.
